questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the university, the course catalogue and the opportunity to explore London!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy through KUnet and emails from the host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails with information on registration and there was an introduction week. However, it was mainly targeted at full time bachelor students and with   a few events targeted at exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was no specific welcome to postgrad students at the faculty. I don't mind reaching out to people myself but I found it strange. A lot of the communications through exchange students was through informal chats and groups on WhatsApp and Instagram.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A large selection of housing around London close to the KCL campuses. There were a lot of options and I was lucky enough to get the cheapest location by Guy's campus close to London Bridge station.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen for me and my 13 neighbors. It was small but worked fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In the flat I was in we were all exchange students, which was lovely! The housing standard in the UK is in general lower than in Denmark so be aware it might be more cold and damp inside. The rent is relatively cheap for London and a great thing is the rooms are furnished and staff who help keep the common spaces clean.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for minimum 4 up to 10 courses - the earlier you apply the more likely you are to secure your dream module. It is important to note however it is good to be flexible as KCL admits you to courses regardless whether they're scheduled at the same time. Remember to check your schedule carefully for classes. I had to change a few classes after the first week as they clashed which is common.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A small but dedicated team helping all exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted. Because of a schedule clash I had to swap two classes which positively surprised me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The module handbook may change between application and official registration. It is very important to flexible about courses and make sures there's more than a handful you are open too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All MA level with full time MA students at KCL.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All classes consisted of a one hour lecture and a one hour seminar. The teaching style was focused on developing logical arguments and critical discussions, which I enjoyed. Compared to UCPH the European & International Studies Department were quite policy-oriented and in general the teachers were very engaging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Union & Identity, Lobbying & Policy-making in the EU, Democratic Legitimacy of International Cooperation and Russia & the European Union.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend European Union & Identity thanks to the passionate module coordinator and with of concepts discussed.l The lobbying course requires a solid understanding of the EU but was very interesting and also included lectures with practitioners. To be honest, I would recommend all of these courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation can be quite expensive but it is possible to get a young adult rail card to save money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I really recommend getting an E-sim and food was a bit cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. There are societies for almost everything open to everyone. There is also a gym on all campuses, a swimming pool available to students, run clubs, yoga and so on. London is a great city and there's something for everyone - whether it's organized by the university or not.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Free yoga if you live through uni accommodation!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking full use of all the discounts available to students in London! At the British Film Institute, you can go to the cinema for £4 and you can watch shows at most theaters for £10 if you're under 25. Then there's also the classics, like Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and so on. Almost all museums are free including the British Museum and the V&A. I really recommend getting a rail card if you want to travel as you get 30% travel throughout the UK. For example, Bath is a lovely city to visit in the Autumn.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy thanks to the language I would say!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is already a boost that everyone speaks English. As a postgrad/master's exchange student you will likely study with people who have just started their full time degrees. KCL is very international and people studying the same courses might be doing different degrees and likely confuse you with being a full time student. Roll with it and suggest going to the pub after class and don't be afraid to show up to mixers and other events which aren't necessarily targeted at exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The brits are both sarcastic and polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be flexible regarding courses, apply for housing as soon as the housing platforms open and have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to be flexible as you can be admitted to courses which clash on the timetable.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved how international the university was and making friends with both locals and exchange students. The best thing was the city - there's always something going on in London and great opportunities to explore the arts, film and music scene.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The scheduling conflict was a bit frustrating and a lot the other post grads were younger than at UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
